newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Standard raises $80 mln five-year loan.
newsitem.headline: Standard raises $80 mln five-year loan.

text.p: Standard Bank London, a subsidiary of Standard Bank Investment Corp, said on Thursday it had become the first South African-owned institution to raise a five-year revolving credit facility.
The bank said the $80 million loan, arranged by a group of international banks on a club deal basis, was priced at 22.5 basis points above the London Interbank Offered rate.

"Because United Kingdom risk is not perceived as high as South African risk, this rate is significantly lower than that obtained for similar facilities to South African banks," it said in a statement.
The transaction had orrginally been launched to raise $50 million, but was oversubscribed.
The arrangers were Barclays Bank, Commerzbank, Deutsche Bank, Dresdner Bank Luxembourg, Fuji Bank, Sanwa Bank, Societe Generale and Standard Chartered Bank.
The loan would be used to further strengthen Standard Bank London's liquidity, it said.
